subject: Satellite hosting: regional availability affirmation + dependency logistics
messages:
From: Marta Larsen <marta.larsen@nordicbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nordicbank.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:12:00 +0200
Subject: Clarification: satellite hosting availability and third‑party dependencies

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we consolidate answers for our EU region RFP, two specific asks came up from our infrastructure and legal teams:

1) Can you confirm which Redwood-managed regions can guarantee no cross-border egress for inference traffic (including KV cache and temporary logs) for EU-only tenancy?
2) Where Redwood relies on third-party services (marketplace billing, telemetry ingestion, mirrors), please list the dependency, its residency, and any compensating controls (e.g., in-region buffering, encryption at rest with customer-managed keys).

We appreciate a matrix-style response and any artifacts (SOC2, network diagram). If you can attach a short availability matrix and a topology diagram, that would speed review.

Best,
Marta
Procurement, NordicBank
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marta Larsen <marta.larsen@nordicbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: satellite hosting availability and third‑party dependencies

Hi Marta,

Thanks — we put together a short matrix and two artifacts for you. Attached: regional-availability-matrix.xlsx (per-tenant residency commitments + fallback behavior), network-topology-diagram.png (high-level call paths), and a SOC2 summary.

Quick answers up front:
- EU-only inference: Redwood can be configured to process and persist inference artifacts entirely in EU-hosted compute and storage (full data residency) for customers on Private or Dedicated plans. Our hosted (multi-tenant) option supports EU data residency for customer data and artifacts when the tenant is provisioned in the EU region but will use global control plane endpoints for billing/metadata unless explicitly contracted otherwise.
- Third‑party dependencies: Marketplace billing (AWS Marketplace) is used only for provisioning/commerce; billing metadata is replicated to Redwood control plane (US‑based) by default. Telemetry ingestion (optional) is routed to regional collectors and can be configured to remain in-region; we offer an in-region buffering layer and customer-configurable retention.

Ben and Marissa are looped for technical and legal attachments. Please let us know if the matrix layout works — we can expand each row into evidence items if needed.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Larsen <marta.larsen@nordicbank.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: satellite hosting availability and third‑party dependencies

Marta / Kimberly —

Following up with the technical breakdown you asked for, summarized here and reflected in the attached matrix:

- Inference compute: runs on customer‑pinned instances in EU regions (Frankfurt, Dublin). KV cache and model shards remain on-region; we do not replicate KV cache out of region unless an explicit failover policy is enabled.
- Ephemeral logs: request traces and ephemeral debug logs are written to regional S3 buckets encrypted with Redwood-managed keys by default. For customers requiring CMK/HSM, we support KMS integrations and rotations.
- Control plane metadata: hostname/service orchestration metadata currently persists in our control plane (us-east-1) for hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer a control-plane localization option with object metadata stored in the customer VPC (recorded in the matrix).
- Marketplace provisioning: AWS Marketplace triggers provisioning events; billing reconciliation records (invoice IDs, order metadata) may traverse to Redwood's billing systems (US). We can supply pseudonymized billing receipts to your finance team and provide an addendum to keep PII out of those flows.

Compensating controls implemented: in-region buffering (24–72h configurable), encryption-in-flight and at-rest, CMK option, and audit-log exports to your storage endpoint.

If you want a sandbox deployment to validate egress behavior, we can stand up a dedicated tenancy in FRA for a two-week run.

- Ben
Principal Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marta Larsen <marta.larsen@nordicbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 18:22:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Clarification: satellite hosting availability and third‑party dependencies

Hi Marta —

Attaching the SOC2 summary and a topology PNG. A couple of evidence notes for procurement/legal:
- SOC2 summary includes the section on data locality and access controls (pages 6–8). Full report can be shared under NDA; see Drive folder link: https://drive.redwood.com/folder/NB-RFP-8342
- The network diagram highlights which telemetry collectors are regionalized — those collectors buffer locally and only forward aggregated telemetry. Raw telemetry forwarding is off by default.

We have also prepared a short appendix (not attached) that lists third-party vendors, residency, and whether they process raw payloads. Happy to drop that into the Drive folder if you want it incorporated into the RFP packet.

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marta Larsen <marta.larsen@nordicbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 15:32:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Clarification: satellite hosting availability and third‑party dependencies

Kimberly / Marissa / Ben —

Thank you — the matrix and artifacts arrived and look good. A few quick follow-ups from legal:

1) Can Redwood commit contractually that, for Dedicated/Private customers, no inference payloads or KV cache will leave the EU region except under pre‑agreed failover conditions?
2) Please provide a redlineable addendum template that limits billing metadata replication outside the EU (we're ok with billing via marketplace but want PII minimization).

If you can drop the addendum draft into the Drive folder and confirm an SLA attestation line we can include in our vendor selection docs, we'll move forward to procurement approval next week.

Best regards,
Marta
Procurement, NordicBank
